onboardingNotes.title: Registration process notes
onboardingNotes.p1: After creating an account, teams should run a baseline readiness check for authentication, success ratio, response latency, and logging quality.
onboardingNotes.p2: Teams should also define release checklists, escalation paths, and rollback plans with clear ownership for each stage.
onboardingNotes.afterRegisterTitle: What You Can Start Right After Registration
onboardingNotes.afterRegisterP1: After registration, you can create proxy extraction settings, monitor real-time usage, manage API credentials, and select proxy types by workload. Use static residential proxies for persistent account sessions, dynamic residential proxies for large-scale collection with retry strategy, and datacenter proxies for high-throughput automation at lower cost.
onboardingNotes.afterRegisterP2: For first-time onboarding, begin with a small traffic test to validate reachability, success rate, and geo targeting before scaling up. This staged rollout helps control budget and catch compatibility or anti-bot issues early.
onboardingNotes.checklist: Registration onboarding checklist: create API credentials, configure endpoint region, validate request success rate, monitor response latency, and scale traffic gradually from staging to production.
onboardingNotes.onboardingProcess: Successful onboarding usually follows a clear sequence: define business goals, map request patterns, configure authentication, validate routing behavior, review error handling, and monitor service quality with consistent metrics.
onboardingNotes.productionReadiness: Production readiness checklist: credential rotation policy, endpoint fallback strategy, request timeout baseline, and weekly quality review cadence.
